title: No clean surface to read a workflow's structured result (_structured_exit / arc vars); bro_wait returns an oversized escaped envelope
wanted_capability: A direct way to read a completed workflow arc's structured output — the `_structured_exit` value and/or named arc vars (e.g. vars.sieve) — without parsing the full bro_wait envelope. Today bro_arc_status returns a snapshot WITHOUT vars, and bro_wait on a workflow task returns an ~81k-char result envelope where the events + node outputs + structured_exit are multi-level JSON-escaped (and it spills to a file over the token cap), so extracting the actual result requires bracket-matching and repeated unescaping. A `bro_arc_result(arc_id)` / `bro_arc_vars(arc_id, keys=[...])` accessor, or having bro_orchestrate_run(await_completion=true) return _structured_exit as a first-class field, would make workflow outputs consumable.
missing_primitive: bro_arc_result / bro_arc_vars accessor, or _structured_exit surfaced as a first-class field on the run/wait result
fallback_used: Parsed the spilled bro_wait tool-result file with python — bracket-matching the sieve object and unescaping multiple levels — to recover the result; hit this 3x this session across the v1/v2/v3 gap-processing runs.
evidence: bro_wait on arc-c60058fe… → 81656-char escaped envelope spilled to file
set_var _structured_exit in .bbox/workflows/gap-processing.json is not directly readable post-run
resolution_note: Three-part fix in src/tools/orchestrate.rs + src/orchestration/mod.rs: (1) new bro_arc_result MCP tool — reads a completed arc's structuredExit, final vars (filterable via keys), arcThreadId, actorSessions, optional nodeOutputs by arcId or task id; (2) the workflow task result envelope no longer duplicates the arc event log (events live in the task event log, readable via bro_status tail), shrinking the bro_wait result from ~81k chars to the structured fields; (3) bro_wait / awaited bro_orchestrate_run lift structuredExit as a first-class field on workflow tasks. Webhook/SSE-ingress arcs are not task-backed and remain out of scope for the accessor (arc thread carries the audit trail).
